ui.title: DocuSmart assistant
ui.greeting: Hi! I'm the DocuSmart assistant. Ask me how to use a tool or anything about the app and the website.
ui.related: You might also find this useful
ui.fallback: I don't have an answer for that. Try asking another way or pick one of these suggestions; if you prefer, write to us and we'll help.
ui.privacyNote: Everything happens in your browser: what you type is never sent anywhere.
ui.aiBadge: ✨ Written by your browser's built-in AI from our knowledge base
ui.sendIntro: Hi, the assistant couldn't answer this question:
ui.sendNote: Your email app opens with the question written in; you decide whether to send it.

entries.a: Hi! How can I help? I can explain how to merge, convert, sign or compress a PDF, create a QR code, use Study mode or tell you how we look after your files.
You're welcome! If you need anything else, I'm here.

I help you find the right tool and use it: PDF (merge, split, sign, compress, protect…), conversions (Word, Excel, image, text), images, ZIP or RAR files, QR codes and Study mode. I also answer questions about privacy, pricing and the Android app.

DocuSmart brings together the tools for your documents: view, convert, merge, sign, scan and protect PDFs, work with images, create QR codes and study with read-aloud. There is DocuSmart Web, which runs in your browser, and the Android app.

q: difference between the website and the app
entries.a: DocuSmart Web works in any browser with nothing to install. The Android app adds a scanner with edge detection, a PIN-protected secure folder, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, OCR, and it works offline.

q: are my files uploaded to a server
is it safe to use with my id documents
entries.a: No. Your files are never uploaded to any server: everything is processed inside your browser (or on your phone, in the app). Neither we nor anyone else receives your documents, so you can use it with contracts, invoices or ID documents.

On the website we only measure usage (for example, "an image was converted to PDF") if you accept in the "Privacy and cookies" notice, which also decides whether ads are shown, and never the content or names of your files. You can change your choice any time under "Analytics preferences" at the bottom of the site.

q: how do I delete my data
entries.a: The website keeps a few things only in your browser for convenience: language, appearance, your notes, and your reading and QR history. None of it is sent anywhere. To delete it, clear the site data for docusmart.online in your browser settings.

q: do I have to sign up
entries.a: No. We don't ask for an account, name, email or phone number, on the website or in the app.

DocuSmart Web is free with no sign-up. The Android app is free too, with ads and some daily limits; for everything unlimited and ad-free there is a monthly or yearly Premium plan (price shown on Google Play) with a 3-day trial when you install, no card needed.

Premium (in the Android app) includes unlimited conversions and PDF tools, no ads, editable PDF to Word, OCR with real, searchable text in scanned PDFs and advanced PDF compression. It is monthly or yearly and managed on Google Play.
When you install the app you get 3 days of every Premium feature, with no card required. When it ends, you keep the free version unless you decide to subscribe.

q: how do I cancel my subscription
entries.a: On Google Play, under Payments & subscriptions, or in the app under Settings → Premium with the "Manage subscription" button. It renews automatically until you cancel it.

q: how many times can I use it
entries.a: There are no daily limits on the website: the only limit is your device memory with very large files. The free app gives you 5 conversions, 3 PDF tool uses and 8 saved scans per day; Premium makes everything unlimited.

q: how large can the file be
entries.a: We don't set a maximum size: since everything happens on your device, its memory is the limit. Very large files may take a bit longer; if it gets stuck, try on a computer or split the file first.
Processing uses your device power. With large files, close other tabs and wait a moment; older phones can be slower. If it stays stuck, reload the page and try again with a smaller file.

Yes. DocuSmart Desktop (the website installed on your computer) downloads the tools by itself and works offline; OCR does after you use it once online. In a regular browser tab, what you've opened before works offline, and the Android app works offline too.

q: does it work on my phone
can I use it on mobile
entries.a: Yes. DocuSmart Web works in the browser of any phone or tablet, and if you use Android, the app does all that and more, offline too.
For now the app is Android-only. On iPhone and iPad you can use DocuSmart Web in Safari or any browser, with nothing to install.

q: where do I get the app
entries.a: The DocuSmart Android app is on Google Play. It is free and adds a scanner with edge detection, a PIN-protected secure folder, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, OCR, and it works offline.
The PIN-protected secure folder is in the Android app: keep your sensitive documents locked there. On the website you can protect a PDF with a password.

actions.label: Open Protect PDF with a password

q: does not work in my browser
entries.a: It works in recent versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, on computers and phones. If something fails, update your browser or try another one.

DocuSmart comes in 12 languages: Spanish, English, Portuguese, German, Russian, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Italian, French, Catalan and Basque. Change it with the globe button at the top or in Settings.
In Settings (the button showing your language) you choose light, dark or system theme, the accent color, the font size and whether you want the animated background.
On the website: image to PDF, JPG, PNG, WebP and BMP; PDF to image, text, Word and Excel; Word and Excel to PDF. The Android app adds more, like PowerPoint to PDF.
In DocuSmart Web tap "Open" on the home screen and choose a PDF, an image or a text file: it opens in the viewer without being uploaded anywhere.
Study mode has read-aloud for your documents (with your choice of voice and speed), notes with images and Pomodoro with statistics.
In Study mode → Reading, load a PDF or text and press "Read": it reads it aloud, highlighting each paragraph. You can choose the voice and speed, highlight parts and resume where you left off.
Reading uses the voices of your browser or system. Turn the volume up, try another voice or another browser (Chrome and Edge include more voices). Some "online" voices need internet.
In Study mode → Notes write your notes and add images. They are stored only in your browser.
In Study mode → Pomodoro you study in 25-minute blocks with breaks; it alerts you when each block ends and shows your statistics.
In QR codes → Read use the camera or choose an image with the code. If it is a protected DocuSmart QR, it asks for the password.
When creating a QR, choose "Protected" and set a password: the content is encrypted and can only be read with DocuSmart (web or app) by someone who knows the password.

actions.label: Open Create and read QR codes

entries.a: In QR codes → History you find the latest QR codes you created or read, stored only in your browser.
If you know the password, use "Unlock PDF" to remove it and work with the file. Without the password it cannot be opened: that is how it protects your documents.
Try "Repair PDF": it rebuilds the file structure so it opens again.

q: how do I save the result
entries.a: When it finishes, tap "Download" and the file goes to your browser downloads folder. On a phone you can also use "Share" to send it to another app.
When a tool finishes, the "Share" button uses your device sharing: pick WhatsApp, email or another app and the file goes straight there, never through our servers.

q: how do I install DocuSmart Desktop
entries.a: DocuSmart Desktop is DocuSmart Web installed on your computer: it opens in its own window, works offline and updates itself. To install it, open the web app in Chrome or Edge and click "Install DocuSmart Desktop" in the sidebar: you'll see the steps for your browser right there.

q: no option to create a desktop icon
entries.a: The desktop icon is created by the browser: in Edge open edge://apps, right-click DocuSmart Desktop and choose "Create desktop shortcut"; in Chrome open chrome://apps, right-click → "Create shortcuts…" and tick "Desktop". For the taskbar: right-click its icon → "Pin to taskbar".

It updates itself when you open it online, with no reinstall and no second copy; if we publish something while it's open, you'll see "Update". If you open it while a window is already open, that window is focused. To uninstall it, open its ⋮ menu (top right) → Uninstall.

Yes. The Guides show you, step by step, how to merge PDFs on your phone, turn photos into a PDF, reduce a PDF's size, sign it without printing, scan with your phone and add a password. They are available in 12 languages.

q: where is the file in drive
entries.a: When a tool finishes, tap "Google Drive" or "Dropbox". The first time, you authorize DocuSmart in a Google or Dropbox window; after that the file goes straight from your browser to your account, without passing through our servers. In Drive it is saved in the DocuSmart folder, and in Dropbox in the DocuSmart folder inside Apps.

q: remove DocuSmart access to google drive
can DocuSmart see my whole drive
what permissions does it ask for
dropbox warning before connecting the app
entries.a: DocuSmart asks for the minimum permission: in Google Drive it only sees the files it saves itself, and in Dropbox only its own folder inside Apps, never the rest of your cloud. To remove access: in Google, myaccount.google.com → Security → Third-party apps & services; in Dropbox, Settings → Connected apps. If Dropbox shows "Before you connect this app", it is a general notice for new apps: you can continue.

q: the file downloads with a different name
how do I rename the result
entries.a: Yes. When a tool finishes, above "Download" there is the "File name" field: type the name you want and the extension (for example, .pdf) is kept automatically. Download, Share, Google Drive and Dropbox all use that name.

q: open the link in the app
I don't want the app to open
open in the browser instead of the app
the link takes me to the app
entries.a: If you have DocuSmart installed on Android, tapping a link to a docusmart.online tool (for example, Merge PDF) opens it directly in the app. If you prefer the browser, long-press the link and choose to open it in the browser, or turn it off in Android Settings → Apps → DocuSmart → Open by default.

q: can the ads see my files
entries.a: Ads keep the website free and only appear if you accept in the "Privacy and cookies" notice; never on the home page or above a tool. Ads cannot see your files, because everything is processed in your browser. You can change your choice any time under "Analytics preferences" at the bottom of the site.

q: check if a file was modified
entries.a: Use "File hash and integrity": it calculates the SHA-256 (or SHA-512, SHA-1, MD5) of any file, checks whether it matches the hash you were given or compares two files. You can also download the list of hashes or a PDF integrity certificate. Everything is calculated in your browser, without uploading anything.

actions.label: Open Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)

q: remove the background from a photo
cut out a person from a photo
entries.a: Use "Remove background": the AI cuts out the person, product or animal and gives you a transparent PNG, with a white background or any color you like. It runs in your browser, so your photos are not uploaded; only the first time is the AI model (about 90 MB) downloaded and stored.

actions.label: Open Remove background from an image

entries.a: Use "Passport & ID photo": pick the size (35 × 45 mm for passports and visas, 2 × 2 in for the US, 30 × 40 mm or any other), frame the face and give it a white background with AI. Download the photo as a 300 dpi JPG or a 4 × 6 in sheet with several copies to print. Everything happens in your browser.
Use "HEIC to JPG": it converts iPhone HEIC photos to JPG (or PNG), several at once and at the quality you choose. It happens in your browser, without uploading your photos.

q: put my logo on a photo
entries.a: Use "Watermark" in Image: put text or your logo on your photos, choose the position (or tiled), size and opacity, and apply it to many images at once. For PDFs there is "Watermark" in PDF.
Write to us at supportdocusmart@docusmart.online or on Facebook or Instagram and we will get back to you.

q: How to merge PDFs in 3 steps
Combine several PDFs into one right in your browser. Free, no sign-up and no uploads: everything is processed on your device.
entries.a:
Combine several PDF files into one and put them in any order. Your documents never leave your device.
1. Choose or drag in the PDFs you want to merge.
2. Order them with the arrows: the first one in the list becomes the start of the document.
3. Press "Merge" and a single PDF with all the pages is downloaded.

q: Are my PDFs uploaded to a server?
entries.a: No. Merging happens inside your browser, with technology that runs on your own device. Nobody else receives your files.

q: How many PDFs can I merge?
entries.a: As many as you need. The only limit is your device's memory: very large documents may take a little longer.
No. Pages are copied as they are, with their original text, images and size.

q: Does it work on my phone?
entries.a: Yes, in any modern browser. And if you use Android, the DocuSmart app does it offline.

q: How to split a PDF in 3 steps
Split a PDF into several files or extract only the pages you need. Free, no sign-up and without uploading the document.
entries.a:
Extract the pages you need or put every page in its own file, right in your browser.
1. Choose the PDF you want to split.
2. Tap the pages you want to keep, type a range such as "1-3, 5" or choose "Each page separately".
3. Download the result: a PDF with the chosen pages or a .zip with one page per file.

q: How do I extract only some pages?
entries.a: Tap them in the thumbnails or type a range, for example "2-4, 7", or "5-" to go from page 5 to the end.
No. A new file is always created; the original stays the same on your device.

q: Is it safe for private documents?
entries.a: Yes. The file isn't uploaded to the internet: the whole process happens in your browser.

q: How to rotate a PDF in 3 steps
Turn PDF pages that ended up sideways or upside down. Rotate one page or all of them, free and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Straighten pages that ended up sideways or upside down, one by one or all at once.
1. Choose the PDF.
2. Tap each page to turn it 90°, or use "Rotate all".
3. Press "Rotate PDF" and download the corrected document.

q: Can I rotate just one page?
entries.a: Yes. Each tap turns that page 90°; the others stay as they were.
Yes, it's saved in the new PDF and will look the same in any reader.

q: Do I need to install anything?
entries.a: No. It works in the browser, without signing up or uploading the file.

q: How to scan a document in 3 steps
Turn photos of documents into a PDF that looks scanned: it finds the page, fixes the perspective and whitens the paper. Several pages and optional OCR. Nothing to install.
entries.a:
Take a photo of your contract, receipt or homework with your phone and DocuSmart turns it into a straight, clean scan, ready to send as a PDF.
1. Press "Take photo" (the camera opens on your phone) or choose photos you already have. Put the page on a dark surface with good light.
2. Check the corners DocuSmart found and choose a filter: Document whitens the paper and removes shadows. Add more pages if you like.
3. Press "Create PDF" (tick "Make the PDF searchable" to be able to search the text) or download the pages as JPG.

q: Do I need to install an app?
entries.a: No. It works in your phone's or computer's browser. If you scan often, the DocuSmart Android app also does it offline.

q: What if it doesn't find the edges well?
entries.a: Drag each corner to the tip of the page, or use "Whole photo". It works best when the paper contrasts with the background (a dark table).
One where, besides the image, the text is recognised (OCR): you can search for words, select them and copy them.

q: Are my photos uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Detection, straightening, filters and OCR all happen inside your browser.

q: How to fill in a PDF form in 3 steps
Fill in the fields of a PDF form in your browser: text, checkboxes, options and lists, with the page in view. Flatten it to send it. Free and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Complete applications, registrations and fillable PDF forms without printing them or installing software, seeing on the page where each answer goes.
1. Choose the PDF form: DocuSmart finds its fields and marks them on the page.
2. Type your answers; tapping a box on the page opens its field, and vice versa.
3. If you are going to send it, tick "Flatten" so the answers become fixed, and press "Fill in the form".
PDFs with fillable fields (AcroForm), which are the vast majority: text boxes, checkboxes, options, drop-down lists and lists. If a PDF has no fields, you can write on top with "Edit PDF".
It makes the answers a fixed part of the document: they look the same in any reader and nobody can change them without leaving a trace. Without flattening, the form stays editable.

q: Can I keep filling it in later?
entries.a: Yes, if you don't flatten it: open the saved PDF again here or in any reader and your answers will still be in the fields.

q: Is my data uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. The form and your answers are processed inside your browser.

q: How to edit a PDF in 3 steps
Write on a PDF, add images, rectangles and circles, highlight text or cover what you don't want seen. Free, no sign-up and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Fill in a form that isn't editable, fix a detail, mark what matters or add your logo, right on the PDF's pages.
1. Choose the PDF.
2. Use the toolbar: Text, Image, Rectangle, Circle, Highlight or Cover. Tap or drag on the page to add them.
3. Adjust size, colour and position, and press "Apply changes".

q: Can I change the text already in the PDF?
entries.a: You can cover it with the "Cover" tool (a white box) and write the new text on top with "Text". The result looks as if you had corrected it.
No: it covers it, but the original text is still inside the file. If you need to truly remove sensitive data, use "Redact PDF".
Three standard PDF families (sans, serif and monospace), in regular or bold, with accented letters. Emojis and other alphabets cannot be saved with those fonts.

q: Are my files uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser, without signing up.

q: How to extract the images from a PDF in 3 steps
Get all the photos and graphics out of a PDF at their original resolution: JPEGs come out identical and the rest as PNG. Download them one by one or as a ZIP, without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Recover the photos, logos and graphics inside a PDF exactly as they were saved, without screenshots or quality loss.
1. Choose the PDF.
2. Press "Find images": all the photos and graphics it contains appear.
3. Pick the ones you want and download them one by one or all together in a ZIP.

actions.label: Open Extract images from a PDF

entries.a: No. JPEG photos are copied byte for byte, identical to the originals, and the rest are saved as PNG, which is lossless.

actions.label: Open Extract images from a PDF

q: How is it different from "PDF to JPG"?
entries.a: "PDF to JPG" turns each whole page into an image. "Extract images" takes out only the photos and graphics inside, each one separately and at its original size.

actions.label: Open Extract images from a PDF

q: Why doesn't anything appear for a scanned PDF?
entries.a: Because in a scan each page is a single large image; for that, use "PDF to JPG". If an image uses an unusual format (JPEG 2000, fax or JBIG2), DocuSmart tells you.

actions.label: Open Extract images from a PDF

q: Are my files uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser.

actions.label: Open Extract images from a PDF

q: How to compare two PDFs in 3 steps
Compare two versions of a PDF and see word by word what was added and removed, with the page of each change. Free and without uploading the files.
entries.a:
Find out in seconds what changed between two versions of a contract, a proposal or a paper, without reading them end to end.
1. Choose the original PDF and the new version.
2. Press "Compare".
3. Review each change: additions in green and removals struck through in red. Download the report if you need it.

q: What kind of changes does it detect?
entries.a: Changes in the text: words, numbers or paragraphs added, removed or modified. If only the line breaks or spacing changed, it doesn't count as a change. Changes in images or layout are not detected.

q: Does it work with scanned documents?
entries.a: A scan is an image and has no text to compare. Run each version through the OCR tool first and compare the searchable PDFs it creates.

q: Does it matter if the pages don't match?
entries.a: No. The whole document is compared, so if a new paragraph pushes everything to the next page, only that paragraph is marked. Each change shows which page it is on in each version.

q: Are my documents uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. The comparison happens inside your browser.

q: How to redact a PDF in 3 steps
Cover names, ID numbers, phone numbers or emails in a PDF and truly remove them, not just hide them under a box. Find and mark everything at once. Free and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Hide personal data before sharing a document: what you cover disappears from the file, it isn't just hidden under a box.
1. Choose the PDF.
2. Search for a word or mark all emails or long numbers; you can also drag on the page to cover any area.
3. Review the pages and press "Redact PDF".

q: Why isn't a black box enough?
entries.a: Because the text is still underneath: anyone can copy it or remove the box. DocuSmart redraws each redacted page as an image, with the areas in black, so the original text disappears from the file.

q: What happens to the rest of the document?
entries.a: Pages without marked areas stay exactly the same. On redacted pages the text can no longer be selected. Also, the new PDF doesn't keep the original's metadata, such as the author or title.

q: Does search work with scanned documents?
entries.a: No: a scan is an image and has no text to search. In that case, mark the areas by dragging on the page.

q: Are my documents uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser; neither the PDF nor what you redact leaves your device.

q: How to sign a PDF in 3 steps
Sign a PDF in your browser: draw your signature with your finger or mouse, type it or upload a photo, and place it wherever you want. Free and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Put your signature on contracts, forms or letters without printing or scanning: draw it, type it or use a photo of your signature on paper.
1. Choose the PDF you want to sign.
2. Create your signature: draw it, type your name or upload a photo of your signature on paper.
3. Drag it into place, adjust the size (you can repeat it on every page) and press "Sign PDF".

It's a simple electronic signature: the image of your signature on the document, like signing by hand. It works for most everyday paperwork; when a digital signature with a certificate is required, you need a certification authority's service.
No. The signature and the PDF are processed inside your browser and are not uploaded to any server. When you close the page, the signature is gone.
Yes. Add the signature to every page you want, or use "Repeat on every page" to put your initials on the whole document.

q: How do I take a good photo of my signature?
entries.a: Sign with dark ink on white paper and take the photo in good light without shadows. DocuSmart removes the white background automatically.

q: Remove margins or keep an area
How to crop a PDF in 3 steps
Crop the pages of a PDF: remove the white margins with one tap or choose by hand the area you want to keep. Free and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Remove extra margins or keep only the part of the page you care about, on every page or on just one.
1. Choose the PDF.
2. Drag the edges of the box on the preview, or press "Remove blank margins".
3. Choose whether to crop all pages or only the current one and press "Crop PDF".
No. Cropping only changes the visible area of each page: text and images stay the same and the text can still be selected.

q: Is what I crop deleted from the file?
entries.a: No: it's hidden, but it's still inside the PDF. If you need to remove sensitive information, cropping isn't enough; use a redaction tool.

q: Can I crop just one page?
entries.a: Yes. Go to that page, adjust the box and choose "Only page" before downloading.

q: Are my files uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Everything happens inside your browser, without signing up.

q: Reduce the size of a PDF
How to compress a PDF in 3 steps
Reduce the size of a PDF in your browser: lossless, or as small as possible for scans. Free, no sign-up and without uploading your file.
entries.a:
Make your PDF smaller to send it by email or WhatsApp. Choose between keeping the quality or shrinking it as much as possible.
1. Choose or drag in the PDF.
2. Pick the level: "Lossless" keeps everything; "Medium" and "High" shrink scans and photos much more.
3. Press "Compress PDF": you'll see how much it shrank and the file is downloaded.

q: Which compression level should I choose?
entries.a: "Lossless" optimises the file without touching the quality and the text stays selectable. If the PDF is a scan or has many photos, "Medium" or "High" shrink it much more, at the cost of turning the text into an image.

q: Is my PDF uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Compression happens inside your browser: the file never leaves your device.
Some PDFs are already optimised. In that case DocuSmart tells you and doesn't download an identical or larger file.
There's no fixed limit; it depends on your device's memory. Very large PDFs may take a little longer.

q: Add a password to a PDF
How to password-protect a PDF in 3 steps
Add a password to a PDF with AES-256 encryption and decide whether it can be printed, copied or modified. Free, no sign-up and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Encrypt your PDF so only someone with the password can open it, and control what can be done with it.
1. Choose the PDF you want to protect.
2. Type the password twice and choose whether to allow printing, copying or modifying.
3. Press "Protect PDF" and the encrypted document is downloaded.

actions.label: Open Protect PDF with a password

entries.a: It uses AES-256 encryption, the strongest PDF standard. It opens in Adobe Acrobat, Chrome, Edge and the DocuSmart app.

actions.label: Open Protect PDF with a password

q: What if I forget the password?
entries.a: It can't be recovered: not even we can open the PDF, because the password never leaves your device. Keep it somewhere safe.

actions.label: Open Protect PDF with a password

q: Is my document uploaded to a server?
entries.a: No. Encryption happens in your browser; neither the file nor the password is sent over the internet.

actions.label: Open Protect PDF with a password

q: How to unlock a PDF in 3 steps
Remove the password or the printing and copying restrictions from a PDF whose password you know. Free, no sign-up and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Remove the password from your own PDF so you don't have to type it every time, or remove printing and copying restrictions.
1. Choose the protected PDF.
2. Type its password. If it opens without a password but won't let you print or copy, leave it empty.
3. Press "Unlock PDF" and a copy without a password is downloaded.

q: Can it open a PDF without knowing the password?
entries.a: No. To remove the opening password you need to know it. What can be removed without a password are the printing and copying restrictions.
Only use it with your own documents or ones you have the right to modify.
No. Everything happens in your browser: neither the PDF nor the password leaves your device.

q: How to repair a PDF in 3 steps
Recover damaged PDFs that won't open or show errors: it rebuilds their internal structure in your browser. Free, no sign-up and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
If a PDF won't open, shows up blank or gives an error, try to recover it by rebuilding its internal structure.
1. Choose the damaged PDF.
2. Press "Repair PDF".
3. A rebuilt copy is downloaded and we tell you whether problems were found.

q: What kind of damage can it repair?
entries.a: Mainly structural problems: a lost or shifted internal cross-reference table, or a damaged end of file. If parts of the content are missing (for example, a download cut off halfway), it may not be recoverable.

q: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?
entries.a: First remove the password with "Unlock PDF" and then repair it.
No. The repair happens in your browser.

q: Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)
How to calculate or verify a file hash in 3 steps
Calculate the SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1 or MD5 hash of any file, verify a checksum or compare two files. Free, with nothing uploaded: it all runs in your browser.
entries.a:
Check that a document hasn't been modified: calculate its digital fingerprint, verify it against the one you were given or compare two files, without them leaving your device.
1. Choose "Calculate", "Verify" or "Compare" and add the file (any type: PDF, photos, ZIP…).
2. Pick the algorithm (SHA-256 recommended) or paste the hash you were given; DocuSmart recognises whether it's SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1 or MD5.
3. Copy the hash, download the list or a PDF integrity certificate, or see whether it matches.

actions.label: Open Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)

q: Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)
entries.a: It's a digital fingerprint of the file: a string of letters and numbers calculated from its content. If the file changes, even by a single byte, the hash is completely different.

actions.label: Open Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)

q: Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)
entries.a: To check that a document you were sent is the same as the original (contracts, tenders, evidence, downloads), to keep a record of what a file looked like on a given date, or to know whether two files are identical without opening them.

actions.label: Open Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)

q: Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)
entries.a: SHA-256 is today's standard and the recommended one. SHA-512 is even longer. MD5 and SHA-1 are fine for comparing with published checksums, but they are no longer considered secure against forgery.

actions.label: Open Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)

q: Calculate and verify a file hash (SHA-256, MD5)

q: How to convert a PDF to PDF/A in 3 steps
Convert a PDF to the PDF/A-2b archival format required by public bodies, courts and universities: fonts and colours included. Free, no sign-up and without uploading the file.
entries.a:
Convert your documents to the standard archival format so they look the same many years from now, without depending on external fonts or software.
1. Choose the PDF.
2. Press "Convert to PDF/A".
3. The PDF/A-2b is downloaded and we tell you what was adjusted to meet the standard.

It's the version of PDF designed for archiving (ISO 19005): the file contains its fonts, colour profile and metadata, and can't depend on anything external. Many procedures with public bodies, courts and universities require it.

q: What level of PDF/A does it create?
entries.a: PDF/A-2b, the most widely used level: it guarantees the document will look the same in the future. We validate it with veraPDF, the PDF Association's reference validator.

q: Does anything in my document change?
entries.a: Missing fonts are embedded and things the standard doesn't allow are removed, such as scripts, attachments or sounds. If a page uses print colours (CMYK) or fonts that aren't in the file, that page is saved as an image.
No. The conversion happens in your browser.

q: How to compress images in 3 steps
Reduce the size of your photos and images without it showing: JPG, PNG and WebP, several at once. Free, no sign-up and without uploading the images to any server.
entries.a:
Make your photos lighter to send them by email or WhatsApp, upload them to a website or save space, with no visible quality loss.

2. Pick the level: low, recommended or maximum.
3. Press "Compress" and download each image or all of them in a ZIP; you'll see how much space you saved.

q: How much smaller do they get?
entries.a: It depends on the photo: with the recommended level, a phone photo usually shrinks by 60% to 90%. If an image was already optimised and can't be reduced, DocuSmart gives you back the original.
With the low and recommended levels, hardly at a glance. The maximum level also scales the image down to 1600 px per side, ideal for messaging and email.

q: What about images with a transparent background?
entries.a: They're saved as WebP, which keeps the transparency and is much smaller than PNG.

q: Are my photos uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Compression happens inside your browser. The photo's hidden data (EXIF), such as GPS location, is also removed.

2. Pick a percentage or type the width and height in pixels (keeping the aspect ratio or not).
3. Press "Resize" and download the result.
Not if you leave "Keep the aspect ratio" ticked: just type the width or the height and the other side is calculated for you.

q: Can I make an image bigger?
entries.a: Yes, up to 200% or the size in pixels you enter, although enlarging doesn't add detail: the photo will look softer.

q: What format is it saved in?

q: Are my photos uploaded to the internet?

2. Pick an aspect ratio (or "Free") and adjust the box by dragging its edges, corners or the whole box.
3. Press "Crop image".

q: Which aspect ratio should I use for a profile picture?
entries.a: 1:1 (square). For covers and videos, 16:9; for stories, 9:16; and for printed photos, 4:3 or 3:4.
No: only the part outside the box is removed; the part you keep retains its resolution.

q: How to make a passport photo in 3 steps
Make your passport, visa or ID card photo: 35 × 45 mm, 2 × 2 in, 30 × 40 mm or any size, with a white background and a 4 × 6 in print sheet. No upload.
entries.a:
Crop your photo to the exact size of a passport, visa or ID card, give it a white background and download it ready to send, or print several copies on one sheet.
1. Choose a front-facing photo with good light (a phone photo works).
2. Pick the size (35 × 45 mm, 2 × 2 in, 30 × 40 mm…), frame the face and choose the background: white, a color or the original.
3. Press "Create photo" and download the single photo or a 4 × 6 in sheet with several copies to print.

It depends on the document and the country: 35 × 45 mm is the most common for passports and visas (European Union, Schengen and much of Latin America); US visas and passports require 2 × 2 inches (51 × 51 mm), and many ID cards use 30 × 40 mm. If you need another one, type it in "Other size". Always check the requirements of the issuing office.

q: How do I get a white background?
entries.a: Choose "White" and the AI separates the person from the background inside your browser. Only the first time is the AI model (about 90 MB) downloaded, and it stays stored. If your photo already has a white background, choose "Original" and nothing is downloaded.

q: Will it print at the right size?
entries.a: Yes. The photo is saved as a 300 dpi JPG with the resolution set in the file, so it prints at the exact size. With "4 × 6 in sheet" you get several copies with a light cutting line, ready for any photo lab or photo printer.

q: Are my photos uploaded to the internet?
entries.a: No. Everything, including the background AI, happens inside your browser: your photo never leaves your device.

q: Is it free? Does it add a watermark?
entries.a: It is free, with no sign-up and no watermark.

entries.a: No. Compression happens inside your browser: your files never leave your device.

RAR (including RAR5), ZIP, 7Z, TAR, GZ, BZ2, XZ and TAR.GZ. The engine is 7-Zip, the same as the desktop application.

No. Everything is extracted inside your browser.
